Here I will walk through cleaning and feature engineering the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet for each of the 3 tabs (BLM assumptions). To run this for each of the tabs, simply replace the file upload which becomes the object called "dat" and replace the tab name of the exported file to the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet will be, then run the entire Rmd.

## II. Unit Conversions

Perform the following unit conversions

-   M -\> uM and nM

-   uM -\> M and nM

-   mol/kg -\> nmol/g and umol/g

That way, we have all variables in units of M, uM, and nM (for dissolved species) or mol/kg and nmol/kg (for biotic ligand-bound elements)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)

# Add a column only if it doesn't already exist
add_if_missing <- function(df, nm, values) {
  if (nm %in% names(df)) df else df %>% mutate(!!nm := values)
}

convert_units_no_dups <- function(dat) {

  # -------------------------
  # 1) Dissolved species: _M, _uM, _nM
  # -------------------------
  diss_vars <- names(dat)[str_detect(names(dat), "(_M|_uM|_nM)$")]
  diss_base <- unique(str_remove(diss_vars, "(_M|_uM|_nM)$"))

  dat <- reduce(diss_base, function(df, base) {

    nm_M  <- paste0(base, "_M")
    nm_uM <- paste0(base, "_uM")
    nm_nM <- paste0(base, "_nM")

    source <- case_when(
      nm_M  %in% names(df) ~ "M",
      nm_uM %in% names(df) ~ "uM",
      nm_nM %in% names(df) ~ "nM",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
    if (is.na(source)) return(df)

    M_vals <- switch(
      source,
      "M"  = df[[nm_M]],
      "uM" = df[[nm_uM]] / 1e6,
      "nM" = df[[nm_nM]] / 1e9
    )

    df %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_M,  M_vals) %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_uM, M_vals * 1e6) %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_nM, M_vals * 1e9)

  }, .init = dat)

  # -------------------------
  # 2) BL variables: *_mol_kg -> *_nmol_kg, *_nmol_g, *_umol_g
  # -------------------------
  bl_molkg <- names(dat)[str_detect(names(dat), "_mol_kg$")]

  dat <- reduce(bl_molkg, function(df, nm) {

    base <- str_remove(nm, "_mol_kg$")

    nm_nmol_kg <- paste0(base, "_nmol_kg")  # mol/kg -> nmol/kg (×1e9)
    nm_nmol_g  <- paste0(base, "_nmol_g")   # mol/kg -> nmol/g  (×1e6)
    nm_umol_g  <- paste0(base, "_umol_g")   # mol/kg -> umol/g  (×1e3)

    vals <- df[[nm]]

    df %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_nmol_kg, vals * 1e9) %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_nmol_g,  vals * 1e6) %>%
      add_if_missing(nm_umol_g,  vals * 1e3)

  }, .init = dat)

  dat
}

# Assign it back if you want to keep using `dat$...`
dat <- convert_units_no_dups(dat)

# quick proof they exist now
names(dat)[str_detect(names(dat), "^BL_.*_(nmol_g|umol_g)$")]
```

Checks

```{r}
# No duplicate column names
anyDuplicated(names(dat))

# Elevation should NOT have uM/nM/M versions
names(dat)[grepl("Relative_elevation_m_", names(dat))]
```

## III. Create New Numeric Variables

### i. Total Bioavailable Element

Total biotic ligand (TBL)-bound trace elements = TBL-element+ TBL-element hydroxide

```{r}
# TBL-Zn in nmol/g
dat$TBL_Zn_nmol_g <- dat$BL_Zn_nmol_g + dat$BL_ZnOH_nmol_g

# TBL-Zn in umol/kg
dat$TBL_Zn_umol_g <- dat$BL_Zn_umol_g + dat$BL_ZnOH_umol_g

# TBL-Zn in mol/kg
dat$TBL_Zn_mol_kg <- dat$BL_Zn_mol_kg + dat$BL_ZnOH_mol_kg

# Check
hist(dat$TBL_Zn_nmol_g)
hist(dat$TBL_Zn_umol_g)
hist(dat$TBL_Zn_mol_kg)
```

### i. Relative Proportion of Bioavailable Element

Relative proportion of element (rel_prop_Zn_nM) = free ion / total measured

```{r}
# Zinc
dat$rel_prop_Zn <- dat$Free_Zn_uM / dat$Zn_uM

# Check
hist(dat$rel_prop_Zn)
```

## IV. Create New Categorical Variables

### i. Stream Type

Distinguish tributaries from the EFPC main stem (within the EFK network)

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Type = if_else(
      Network == "EFK",
      "Main Stem",
      "Tributaries"
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("Main Stem", "Tributaries"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Type)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Type))
```

### ii. Development

Categorizing developed land use and land cover (LULC) will be based on a modified version of the MRLC National Land Cover Database Class Legend and Description. Our categories will be as follows

-   \<49% developed LULC = low intensity

-   50-79% developed LULC = medium intensity

-   \>80% developed LULC = high intensity

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Development = case_when(
      Developed_lulc < 50 ~ "Low",
      Developed_lulc >= 50 & Developed_lulc < 80 ~ "Medium",
      Developed_lulc >= 80 ~ "High"
    ) %>% 
      factor(levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Development)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Development))
```

### iii. Relative Elevation

To classify relative elevation (m) into categories, we first have to omit 0 values which correspond to the Main Stem

```{r}
tribs <- dat %>%
  filter(Relative_elevation_m != "0")
```

Now we'll first inspect the distribution of relative elevation distribution

```{r}
hist(tribs$Relative_elevation_m, breaks = 386, xaxt = "n")   # remove default axis

axis(
  side = 1,
  at = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = max(tribs$Relative_elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    by = 5                                           # tick every 5 km2
  )
)
```

Check its quartiles

```{r}
summary(tribs$Relative_elevation_m)
```

Breaks at 1st and 3rd quartiles

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Relative_elevation = case_when(
      Relative_elevation_m == 0 ~ "0 m",
      Relative_elevation_m < 2.1 ~ "<2.1 m",
      Relative_elevation_m >= 2.1 & Relative_elevation_m <= 10.5 ~ "2.1-10.5 m",
      Relative_elevation_m > 10.5 ~ ">10.5 m",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("<2.1 m","2.1-10.5 m",">10.5 m", "0 m"))
  )

# Check
summary(dat$Relative_elevation)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Relative_elevation))
```

## V. Save to Excel

Bring new variables describing stream inherent characteristics to the front

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  relocate(Type,
           Development,
           Relative_elevation,
           .before = pH)

# Check
head(dat)
```

Check the structure one last time before saving

```{r}
str(dat)
```

Save to excel as a clean version of the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path  <- "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean.xlsx"
sheet_name <- "HA 80% Closed System"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Create workbook if it doesn't exist, otherwise load it
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  wb <- createWorkbook()
} else {
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# If sheet already exists → remove it
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (sheet_name %in% names(wb)) {
  removeWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Create fresh sheet and write data
# ---------------------------------------------------------
addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)

writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = sheet_name,
  x = dat,
  colNames = TRUE
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Save workbook
# ---------------------------------------------------------
saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file_path,
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Now repeat this for

-   HA 80% Closed System

-   HA 10% Open System

By replacing the name of the sheet imported and the final excel sheet saved to the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet (first and last code blocks)
